CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left lower back pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male with history of back surgery (microdiscectomy) in November 2020 for a disk herniation that was compressing the spinal thecal sac. He had severe nerve pain and leg pain at that time and was treated with high-dose gabapentin, which he found difficult to withdraw from. He now presents with left-sided lower back pain. Pain is exacerbated by bending over and occurs randomly. Location of pain sometimes shifts to the right side depending on the day, generally around the area of his prior surgery. Patient reports that stretching helps alleviate symptoms. He has been taking ibuprofen 800mg daily for pain management. Denies icing the area. No pain radiating down the legs.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies leg pain, nerve pain, or other systemic complaints.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Back surgery (microdiscectomy) November 2020 for disk herniation compressing spinal thecal sac

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen 800mg daily
History of high-dose gabapentin (prior to current visit)

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not documented

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Flexion: No pain with forward flexion currently
Extension: No pain with extension
Standing: Pain with weightbearing while standing
Palpation: Pain with palpation to left side around L5; no pain with palpation to right side
Dorsiflexion: Normal strength, able to push against resistance
Range of motion: Normal
Neurological: No pain down legs

RESULTS
X-ray of spine: No fractures or abnormalities of spinal bone; surgical site shows proper healing

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Assessment: Muscle pull with spinal misalignment at surgical site.
Plan: 
1. Discontinue ibuprofen 800mg daily
2. Initiate meloxicam for improved pain management
3. Physical therapy referral
4. Referral to pain management for evaluation and management strategies
5. Demerol prescribed
